<a id="create-phase-filter"></a>

### Create phase filter

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** make a new phase filter under a given name, and set each phase status in it to By Category, Overridden or Not Displayed.

Makes a new phase filter - Manage, Phasing, Phase Filters, New - under the name given, and sets each phase status in it to By Category, Overridden or Not Displayed. A name already used refuses and names that filter; each status is read back. The Graphic Overrides tab has no API and is set by hand.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **filter name** - text<br>**new display** - text; optional, left out means *leave*<br>**existing display** - text; optional, left out means *leave*<br>**demolished display** - text; optional, left out means *leave*<br>**temporary display** - text; optional, left out means *leave* |
| **You get** | phase filter id, created, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `CREATE_PHASE_FILTER` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
3. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"create a phase filter called As-Built"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"make a new phase filter"* · *"add a phase filter that hides demolished"*

<a id="report-phase-filters"></a>

### Report phase filters

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** the project's phase filters by exact name, and how each one shows each phase status.

Lists the phase filters of the project - the Phase Filters tab of Manage, Phasing - by exact name, with each phase status shown By Category, Overridden or Not Displayed, whether it is one of Revit's own, and how many views use it. Name one to read that one alone.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Answers a question (`READ`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **filter name** - text; optional, left out means *all* |
| **You get** | phase filter names, phase filter ids, filter count, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `REPORT_PHASE_FILTERS` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"what phase filters are in this project"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
3. Heron answers in the chat. Nothing in the model changes.

Other ways to ask: *"list the phase filters"* · *"how is the Show Complete phase filter set"*

<a id="set-element-phase"></a>

### Set element phase

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** put these elements on a different phase.

Moves elements onto a different created-phase, or sets when they are demolished. **Before this, *"set the phase"* resolved to SET_ELEMENT_WORKSET** - a write, to the wrong property, that looks like it worked. A workset and a phase are both invisible groupings that decide what a view shows, and confusing them silently moves work into another team's ownership while leaving it in the wrong phase. **Changing a phase changes what every view shows, not just this one.** A view has a phase and a phase filter; an element on the wrong phase vanishes from some views, appears as demolished in others, and comes out of the wrong schedule. That is the whole point of phases and it is why this is a bulk change worth confirming before running. **Demolishing is a separate field from creating**, and setting the wrong one is how existing work disappears. Which one is being set is required, never inferred from the phase's name.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **Works on** | what is selected in Revit: elements |
| **You say** | **phase id** - the NAME of the thing, never its number - "Level 1" for a levelId. The field's own name says which kind<br>**which phase** - text |
| **You get** | changed |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `SET_ELEMENT_PHASE` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Select what it works on in Revit (elements) - or name it in the same request, and Heron finds it first.
3. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
4. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"set the phase"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
5. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"move these to New Construction"* · *"change the phase on these"*
